* {{hyph|en|cost}}

===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:costen<pos:v><ety:bor<fro:coster>>|text=++|tree=1}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb|~s|~ing|~<id:verb>,~ed<l:proscribed><qq:see usage note>}} {{cln|en|irregular simple past forms|irregular past participles}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|ditransitive}} To [[incur]] a [[charge]] of; to require payment of a (specified) [[price]].
#: {{ux|en|This shirt '''cost''' $50, while this was cheaper at only $30.}}
#: {{ux|en|It will '''cost''' you a lot of money to take a trip around the world.}}
#* {{RQ:Belloc Lowndes Lodger|I|0016
|passage=Thus the red damask curtains which now shut out the fog-laden, drizzling atmosphere of the Marylebone Road, had '''cost''' a mere song, and yet they might have been warranted to last another thirty years. A great bargain also had been the excellent Axminster carpet which covered the floor;{{nb...}}.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|ditransitive}} To cause something to be lost; to cause the [[expenditure]] or [[relinquishment]] of.
#: {{ux|en|Trying to rescue the man from the burning building '''cost''' them their lives.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|title=How our home delivery habit reshaped the world| author=Samanth Subramanian| date=November 21 2019| url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2019/nov/21/how-our-home-delivery-habit-reshaped-the-world| passage=the packaging of home-delivered products now accounts for 30% of the solid rubbish the US generates annually, and the cardboard alone '''costs''' 1bn trees. |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013090810/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2019/nov/21/how-our-home-delivery-habit-reshaped-the-world|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Much Ado About Nothing|act=II|scene=i|passage=though it '''cost''' me ten nights' watchings}}
# To [[require]] to be [[borne]] or [[suffer]]ed; to [[cause]].
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=1|passage=to do him wanton rites, which '''cost''' them woe|year=1873}}
#* {{quote-av|en|year=1977|title=w:Star Wars
|passage=LUKE: "That little droid is going to '''cost''' me a lot of trouble."}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|colloquial}} To cost (a person) a great deal of money or suffering.
#: {{ux|en|I can give you the names, but it'll '''cost''' you.}}
#: {{ux|en|That's going to '''cost''' you!}}

=====Usage notes=====
* The simple past and past participle is {{m|en||cost}}, with regularly-expected {{m|en|costed}} generally being {{lg|proscribed}}; this contrasts with {{m|en|cost|id=estimate|t=to calculate or estimate costs|ng=see {{senseno|en|estimate|etym=1}}}}, which does have the regular past form {{m|en|costed}}.

===Etymology 2===
{{ety|en|id=amount|:inh|enm:cost<pos:n><ety:deverbal<enm:costen<pos:v><t:to cost><ety:bor<fro:coster>>>>|text=2|tree=1}}

====Noun====
{{wp}}
{{en-noun|~}}

# Amount of [[money]] (or [[time]], etc.) that is [[required]] or used.
#: {{ux|en|The total '''cost''' of the new complex was an estimated $1.5 million.}}
#: {{ux|en|We have to cut '''costs''' if we want to avoid bankruptcy.}}
#: {{ux|en|The average '''cost''' of a new house is twice as much as it was 20 years ago.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-08|volume=407|issue=8839|page=55|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/business/21579011-president-proposes-new-round-intellectual-property-reform-obama-goes-troll-hunting Obama goes troll-hunting]| passage=According to this saga of intellectual-property misanthropy, these creatures [patent trolls] roam the business world, buying up patents and then using them to demand extravagant payouts from companies they accuse of infringing them. Often, their victims pay up rather than face the '''costs''' of a legal battle.}}
# A negative [[consequence]] or loss that occurs or is required to occur.
#: {{ux|en|Spending all your time working may earn you a lot of money at the '''cost''' of your health.}}
#: {{ux|en|The army won the battle decisively, but at a '''cost''' of many lives.}}

===Etymology 4===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*ǵews-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|cost}}, from {{inh|en|ang|cost||option, choice, possibility, manner, way, condition}}, from {{der|en|non|kostr||choice, opportunity, chance, condition, state, quality}}, from  {{der|en|gem-pro|*kustuz||choice, trial}} (or {{der|en|gem-pro|*kustiz||choice, trial}}), from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ǵéwstus||to enjoy, taste}}.

Cognate with {{cog|is|kostur}}, {{cog|de|-}} dialectal {{m|de|Kust||taste, flavour}}, {{cog|nl|kust||choice, choosing}}, {{cog|frr|kest||choice, estimation, virtue}}, {{cog|fy|kêst||article of law, statute}}, {{cog|ang|cyst||free-will, choice, election, the best of anything, the choicest, picked host, moral excellence, virtue, goodness, generosity, munificence}}, {{cog|la|gustus||taste}}. {{doublet|en|gusto}}, and related to {{m|en|choose}}.
